title: aidd library standard
description: The YAML front matter of one opinionated standard in aidd's library (`standards/<group>/<topic>.md`): one choice a pack or practice skill leaves open, with its why, its tool and checked version, and the tests that enforce it. `aidd standard add` copies the file into a project. Industry standards live only in the registry (`schemas/roles.json`), never here.

id.description: Stable id, `<group>/<topic>`, such as `python/ruff-lint-format`. It matches the file's path under `standards/`. A renamed id stays in `standards/renames.yaml`.

type.description: Always `opinionated`: a choice a team commits to. An industry standard lives in the registry and is only waived per project.

fills.description: The open choices it answers, each `<pack or skill>:<choice>`, such as `ci-pipeline:linter`. Required for a library standard, so it cannot overlap a pack.

default.description: Whether it is aidd's default for each choice it fills, in its ecosystem. The library may hold several options for one choice; exactly one active option per choice and ecosystem is the default. A project adopts one of them.

implements.description: The pack or skill rule it puts to work, `<pack or skill>:<rule>`, such as `product-defaults:dev_basics`. It links the rule and never restates it.

roles.description: aidd-team roles that read it before their step, or `*` for every role.

when_changed.description: Load it, and run its tests, only for a change that touches one of these paths.

why.description: Why this option, in one or two sentences.

reviewed.description: The day the choice was last judged still the right one for its slot: a judgment, which no source can carry. `checked` is the other kind of date, a fact re-read at its source. Due again after a year when established, after 90 days when emerging.

maturity.description: Established tools are reviewed yearly; emerging ones every 90 days.

tool.description: The tool it chooses, and where its releases are published. The weekly standards check reads that feed and flags a newer major than `checked_version`. It reads stable releases only and, for `version_policy: latest_lts`, the newest LTS release where the feed marks one.

name.description: The tool's name, such as `ruff`. One library standard owns each tool.

registry.description: The release feed: PyPI, npm, crates.io, Maven Central, NuGet, the Go module proxy, or GitHub releases for a package; for a language toolchain, its official feed: go.dev, nodejs.org, the .NET release index, Adoptium, or python.org.

package.description: The name in that feed: a package, `group:artifact` on Maven Central, a module path on the Go proxy, or `owner/repo` on GitHub. A toolchain feed takes one fixed name: `go`, `node`, `sdk` or `runtime` (.NET), `temurin`, or `cpython`. Its form is checked per feed, so it can only name a package there.

version_policy.description: Which version a project uses. The version itself is a field, never prose.

checked_version.description: The newest release read at the source on the `checked` day. Never typed from memory.

checked.description: The day `checked_version` was read at the tool's release feed, or the standard's claim at its source. It needs `source` and `evidence`.

checked_by.description: Who read `source` on the `checked` day: `agent:<harness>/<model>` for an agent's check, or a person's identity (`@login` or `email:<address>`, as an Approver is named) for a person's review. It sets the trust tier that `aidd standard list` and `aidd eval standards` show: an entry is checked by an agent until a person reviews it, and an entry without `checked_by` counts as an agent's check.

source.description: The official page where `checked_version` or the standard's claim was read on the `checked` day. Required with `checked`.

evidence.description: The sentence read at `source` on the `checked` day, quoted exactly, so the date is never a bare assertion. Required with `checked`.

pin.description: The version the `enforced_by` commands run, such as `0.16.10`.

alternatives.description: Other valid options for the same choice, by name. A company picks one through `standards_policy.replace`.

status.description: `deprecated`: kept so projects that copied it hear about it; `replaced_by` names the successor.

replaced_by.description: The library standard that replaces a deprecated one.

enforced_by.description: `tests` templates. `aidd standard add` writes each one, so the gate runs it on every change its `when_changed` matches.

choice_ref.description: An open choice, `<pack or skill>:<choice id>`, such as `ci-pipeline:linter`.
